headline_marked: [[Xbox Series X can now run PlayStation 5 games]], but with a strict 5GB memory limit
headline: Xbox Series X can now run PlayStation 5 games, but with a strict 5GB memory limit
summary: Developer Devran Cosmo Uenal ported the KytyPS5 emulator to Xbox Series X, allowing PS5 games like Quake II to run, but only in Developer Mode with a 5GB memory cap.
details: Developer Devran Cosmo Uenal demonstrated PS5X, an Xbox port of the KytyPS5 emulator, running PlayStation 5 games on an Xbox Series X. His video showed Quake II booting and being played with an Xbox controller, with three other PS5 titles also working.

The significant catch is that PS5X only functions in the console's official Developer Mode, which imposes a strict 5GB memory limit on games. This restriction unfortunately excludes the vast majority of current-generation PS5 titles from being playable.

The possibility arises from the consoles' closely matched AMD hardware, featuring eight Zen 2 CPU cores, RDNA 2 graphics, and 16GB GDDR6 memory. PS5 games are compiled for the same x86-64 architecture as PCs, allowing KytyPS5 to act as a compatibility layer rather than a full hardware recreation.

A major technical hurdle is the translation of PS5's Vulkan graphics commands to DirectX 11/12, as Xbox Developer Mode doesn't support Vulkan 1.3. This means fixes made to the KytyPS5 PC renderer require adaptation for PS5X. AI was reportedly involved in this translation work.

Uenal describes PS5X as a "research project" for "running PS5 homebrew and game backups" in Developer Mode, claiming no PS5 firmware or decryption keys are included. The project operates within a legal grey area, reminiscent of the Switch emulator Yuzu, which faced a major lawsuit from Nintendo.

Currently, PS5X runs the PS5 versions of GEX Trilogy, Hellboy: Web of Wyrd, Marvel Cosmic Invasion, and Quake II, all compatible with Xbox controllers and some with sound. Quake II reportedly runs between 25-45 frames per second, though no PS5 exclusives have been shown running yet.

The 5GB memory limit in Xbox Developer Mode is a significant constraint, compared to the 13.5GB available to retail Series X games. This severely limits the scope of PS5X, making it unsuitable for large, modern titles.

Microsoft previously blocked emulators in Xbox's normal retail mode in 2023, citing a store policy against emulating other game systems. This led to suspensions for players who found workarounds, reinforcing the need for projects like PS5X to operate within Developer Mode.

headline_marked: [[Google's SynthID AI detector]] now open to all for images, video, audio
headline: Google's SynthID AI detector now open to all for images, video, audio
summary: Google's SynthID Detector is now publicly available, allowing anyone to check if images, videos, or audio files were generated by AI models from Google, OpenAI, NVIDIA, and Kakao by scanning for imperceptible watermarks.
details: Google has made its SynthID Detector publicly available at SynthID.com, enabling anyone to verify if an image, video, or audio file has been created or manipulated by AI. This tool scans for an imperceptible digital watermark embedded in AI-generated content.

SynthID was initially introduced in 2023, with Google's Gemini AI model embedding these watermarks in all its creations. The detector tool was previously limited to certain researchers and journalists, but is now accessible to the general public.

To use the tool, users simply visit SynthID.com, upload their media file, and wait a few seconds for a yes/no result indicating if a watermark was found. This offers a more reliable verification method than asking a generative AI model directly.

The detector can identify watermarks from Google's Gemini, as well as content from SynthID partners like OpenAI, NVIDIA, and Kakao. Apple also participates in SynthID, with detector support for its creations currently in development.

By checking for a specific watermark rather than analyzing content patterns, SynthID Detector aims to eliminate false positives. However, it cannot detect media generated by AI models that do not utilize the SynthID watermarking system, such as Meta's tools.

Google states that SynthID signatures are designed to persist even after content is edited. To prevent potential misuse, users are reportedly limited to around 10 checks per day and must log in with a Google, OpenAI, or Apple account.
